c.tagline: A castle-crowned capital where the Danube meets old-world charm.

taxi.fareNote: Metered fares roughly €1.30-1.50/km with a €3-4 base/starting fee; ride-hail apps like Bolt are cheaper and more transparent than street taxis.

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU emergency number and reaches all services with English-speaking operators.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Use ride-hailing apps or official taxis to dodge notorious street-taxi overcharging, and mind pickpockets in Old Town crowds and around the main station at night.

hood_desc: The historic heart with cobblestone lanes, cafes, and the castle nearby; best for first-time visitors who want to walk everywhere and be near sights and nightlife.
A riverside district across the Danube with the SNP Bridge/UFO tower and Sad Janka Kráľa park; suits budget travelers and those wanting green space with a short tram/bus ride to downtown.
A mixed residential-business district with the Slovak modern architecture and Bonbon/Central shopping malls; good for business travelers and longer stays wanting local, less touristy life.
Convenient for rail travelers arriving by train or bus, with easy tram access to Old Town; suits transit-focused visitors and those on a budget near the station.
Quieter, leafy areas along the Danube near Devín Castle, popular with those seeking nature, hiking, and a slower pace outside the tourist core.
lodging: Grand Hotel River Park, a Luxury Collection Hotel

water.note: Meets EU drinking water standards and is safe straight from the tap.

transit.pay: Buy tickets in advance via the IDS BK mobile app, at ticket machines (DPB kiosks) at major stops, or from newsagents; tickets must be validated on boarding trams/buses. Contactless bank-card tap-on payment is also available on most trams and buses. There are no ticket sales on board most vehicles.
transit.hours: Trams and buses run roughly 4:30am-11:30pm, with a reduced night bus network running through the night on key routes.
transit.note: The whole city center is very walkable, so many visitors rely on trams/buses only for airport transfers or longer trips to Devín or Petržalka.

air: Vienna International Airport (VIE, ~50 min away by bus, often used for cheaper flights)
train: Bratislava hlavná stanica (Main Station) - connections to Vienna, Prague, Budapest, Košice
bus: Bratislava Autobusová stanica (Mlynské Nivy) - Flixbus, RegioJet, Slovak Lines regional/international coaches
ferry: Danube river cruise/hydrofoil services to Vienna and Budapest (seasonal)

tip.r: Rounding up or adding 5-10% at restaurants is appreciated but not mandatory; often done by telling the server the total amount including tip rather than leaving cash on the table.

food.name: Bryndzove halusky
food.desc: Slovakia's national dish: soft potato dumplings folded through sharp sheep's bryndza cheese and scattered with crisp bacon and its fat.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Warren of countryside-style rooms serving generous halusky at student prices.

places.name: Bratislava Flagship Restaurant
places.note: Huge former theatre turned Slovak restaurant; a dependable first taste of halusky.

places.name: Zylinder Cafe Restaurant
places.note: Cosy Austro-Hungarian styled dining room doing the classic version well.

food.name: Kapustnica
food.desc: Sour cabbage soup with smoked sausage, dried mushrooms, prunes and paprika; a Christmas Eve tradition eaten all winter as a meal in itself.

places.name: Zylinder Cafe Restaurant
places.note: Frequently named the best kapustnica in the centre; served in a bread bowl option.

places.name: Koliba Kamzik
places.note: Log-cabin restaurant above the city, the traditional setting for cabbage soup.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Big bowls of smoky kapustnica alongside the rest of the Slovak repertoire.

food.name: Lokse
food.desc: Thin potato flatbreads griddled dry, then served savoury with duck fat, goose liver or cabbage, or sweet with poppy seed and jam.

places.name: Lokse pod Kamzikom
places.note: Specialist hut on the forest hill above town devoted to lokse and roast goose.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Sweet and savoury lokse on the menu year-round, not just at goose season.

places.name: Viecha U Sedliaka
places.note: Small low-key local tavern opposite Slovak Pub with homely Slovak plates.

food.name: Treska
food.desc: Bratislava's cod salad: shredded white fish in mayonnaise with onion and carrot, piled onto bread rolls and eaten as a snack or starter.

places.name: Stara Trznica
places.note: Old market hall delis sell treska by weight; Saturday market days are best.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Serves treska as a cheap starter alongside beer, the way locals order it.

places.name: Bratislava Flagship Restaurant
places.note: Keeps the old Pressburg deli classics on a long traditional menu.

food.name: Vyprazany syr
food.desc: A thick slab of edam breadcrumbed and deep-fried, served with chips and a mound of tartar sauce; Slovakia's beloved comfort plate.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Textbook fried-cheese-and-chips plate, generous and inexpensive.

places.name: Viecha U Sedliaka
places.note: Quiet local room where the fried cheese comes without any tourist framing.

places.name: Bratislava Flagship Restaurant
places.note: Reliable central kitchen for the fried classics with fast service.

food.name: Bratislavske rozky
food.desc: Protected local pastry: a crescent or horseshoe of rich yeast dough filled with poppy seed or walnut paste, glossy and marbled on top.

places.name: Stara Trznica
places.note: Market-hall bakers sell the poppy and walnut crescents fresh at weekends.

places.name: Konditorei Kormuth
places.note: Ornate hand-painted cafe serving Pressburg-era pastries with coffee.

places.name: Old Town bakeries
places.note: Neighbourhood pekaren counters around the centre bake them daily and cheaply.

food.name: Small Carpathian wine
food.desc: Crisp whites from the hills just north of the city - Gruner Veltliner, Riesling and the native Devin - plus cloudy young burciak each autumn.

places.name: Vinoteka Sv. Urban
places.note: Long-running wine shop and bar focused on Slovak growers, with tastings by the glass.

places.name: Stara Trznica
places.note: Market hall wine stalls pour Small Carpathian bottles on market days.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Easy place to try Slovak wine by the glass alongside a plate of halusky.

food.name: Borovicka
food.desc: Clear juniper spirit distilled in the Slovak mountains, drunk as a chilled shot before or after a meal; herbal Tatratea is the modern rival.

places.name: Slovak Pub
places.note: Full range of Slovak spirits including borovicka and Tatratea at low prices.

places.name: Viecha U Sedliaka
places.note: Neighbourhood tavern where locals take borovicka with their beer.

places.name: Old Town cellar bars
places.note: Cellar pubs around Michalska and Venturska pour shots of both spirits late.

landmarks: Bratislava Castle
This whitewashed hilltop fortress overlooking the Danube is Bratislava's defining silhouette, offering sweeping views across the river into Austria and Hungary.
St. Martin's Cathedral
This Gothic coronation church crowned nineteen Hungarian kings and queens, and its slender spire remains a striking anchor of the Old Town skyline.
Michael's Gate
The last surviving gate of Bratislava's medieval fortifications, its tower and passageway offer a photogenic gateway into the cobbled Old Town.
Čumil (The Watcher)
A whimsical bronze sewer worker peeking out from a manhole is one of the world's most photographed street sculptures and a beloved Old Town photo op.
Church of St. Elizabeth (Blue Church)
Drenched in pastel blue from spire to walls, this Art Nouveau church is an unmistakably whimsical and Instagram-famous landmark unlike any other in Europe.
Old Town Hall
Bratislava's oldest town hall complex blends Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque styles around a charming courtyard, now home to the city history museum.
Primate's Palace
This elegant Neoclassical palace with an allegorical rooftop statue group hosted the signing of the historic Peace of Pressburg treaty in 1805.
Devín Castle
Perched dramatically on a rocky cliff where the Danube and Morava rivers meet, these ancient ruins evoke over a thousand years of Slavic history.
UFO Observation Deck (Most SNP Bridge)
A saucer-shaped restaurant and viewing platform perched atop a bridge pylon delivers a futuristic, panoramic vista over the Danube and Old Town.
Slavín Memorial
This towering war memorial and cemetery honoring Soviet soldiers sits on a hilltop above the city, offering solemn grandeur and sweeping views.

train.note: Vienna trains leave from both the Main Station and Petržalka. The seasonal night train to Split now starts in Vienna — hop the 1-hour train there to board it.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches leave from the modern Nivy station under the Nivy mall; Vienna Airport buses run round the clock, every 30–60 minutes.

ferry.note: The high-speed Danube catamaran to Vienna (~1h 15m) runs several times daily from the Old Town riverbank, late March to late October. There is no longer any boat service to Budapest.

half.name: Vienna
half.blurb: Imperial city of grand palaces, coffeehouses, and centuries of classical music.

half.name: Brno
half.blurb: Moravian city famed for its hilltop fortress and vibrant student atmosphere.

full.name: Budapest
full.blurb: Danube-straddling capital famed for thermal baths, grand architecture, and river views.

full.name: Ostrava
full.blurb: Czech industrial city known for its coal-mining heritage and lively music scene.

full.name: Graz
full.blurb: Historic Austrian city with a red-roofed old town and lively university culture.

full.name: Linz
full.blurb: Austrian city on the Danube known for its arts scene, industry, and riverside old town.

full.name: Gliwice
full.blurb: Industrial Silesian city known for coal-mining heritage and a striking wooden radio tower.

full.name: Zabrze
full.blurb: Upper Silesian city known for its coal-mining heritage and industrial landmarks.

full.name: Bielsko-Biala
full.blurb: Southern Polish city known for its historic textile industry and Beskid Mountain backdrop.
